bull.b: Very low leverage reduces fixed financial obligations and preserves flexibility while Chemomab advances its clinical programs. A largely debt-free structure limits interest-related pressure and may make future financing or strategic transactions easier to manage, even though losses remain substantial.

The improvement in annual losses and reduced cash burn indicates some expense discipline as the company progresses through development. Although Chemomab remains unprofitable and cash consuming, a slower rate of deterioration can extend financial flexibility and support continued investment in its pipeline.

FDA feedback consistent with the planned Phase 2 program reduces uncertainty around the trial’s development framework and supports the progression of nebokitug into a broader indication. This provides a clearer regulatory path for the lead asset and could strengthen the pipeline’s strategic value.

bear.b: The absence of revenue means Chemomab has not yet demonstrated commercial traction or an operating model capable of funding itself. Its near-term financial profile therefore depends on clinical progress and external capital rather than customer receipts, increasing sensitivity to development outcomes.

Sustained negative operating and free cash flow requires ongoing access to financing to fund research, development, and corporate operations. Even with improved burn in 2025, continued cash consumption can constrain the pace of pipeline investment and expose the company to financing risk.

The proposed redomiciliation and Scipher merger remain dependent on multiple approvals and execution steps, while related financing and clinical-development challenges add uncertainty. Delays or failure to complete the transaction could disrupt strategic plans and complicate access to needed capital.
